title: India-Australia Sign New Defence Declaration to Deepen Indo-Pacific Cooperation
summary: During PM Modi's visit to Australia, India and Australia unveiled a new defence declaration aimed at deepening cooperation in the Indo-Pacific region. The two countries agreed to deepen ties across nuclear, maritime, and mineral sectors. The visit also featured PM Modi addressing the Indian diaspora in Melbourne, highlighting India's growth, Operation Sindoor, Make in India, and India's global humanitarian role.
exam_angle: India-Australia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and the Quad framework are recurring themes in GS Paper 2 (IR). The Indo-Pacific security architecture and bilateral defence cooperation are key exam topics.
key_facts: New defence declaration signed during PM Modi's Australia visit (July 2026)
Cooperation spans nuclear, maritime, and mineral sectors
India-Australia relationship is a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership
Part of broader Indo-Pacific strategy; both nations are Quad members

title: India-Australia Bilateral Highlights: Early Trade Pact, AUD 500 Million Investment, Uranium Deal, Clean Energy
summary: PM Modi's visit to Australia resulted in several key bilateral outcomes including progress on an early trade pact, an AUD 500 million investment commitment, a uranium supply deal that could transform India's nuclear energy future, and cooperation on clean energy. The uranium deal is significant as India seeks to diversify nuclear fuel sources to power its expanding civil nuclear programme. New Zealand PM Christopher Luxon also hailed a separate trade pact with India, noting '57% tariff-free from day one'.
exam_angle: India's civil nuclear programme, uranium sourcing, and bilateral trade agreements are important for GS Paper 2 (IR) and GS Paper 3 (Economy). The Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG) context and India's energy security are linkable concepts.
key_facts: AUD 500 million investment commitment from Australia to India
India-Australia uranium supply deal agreed in principle
Early Harvest/interim trade pact discussions progressed
New Zealand-India trade pact: 57% tariff-free access from day one

title: Navy's Drishti-10 UAV (Hermes-900 Platform) Crashes Near Porbandar, Gujarat; Inquiry Ordered
summary: The Indian Navy's Drishti-10 Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) crashed near Porbandar, Gujarat during a training sortie. No loss of life was reported and an inquiry has been ordered into the incident. This is reported to be the second mishap involving the Hermes-900 platform, which India procures from Israel's Elbit Systems. The Drishti-10 is a maritime patrol drone used for surveillance over the Arabian Sea.
exam_angle: India's indigenisation and procurement of UAV/drone technology for defence is an important GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech/Defence) topic. The Drishti-10 is a key asset in India's maritime domain awareness strategy.
key_facts: Drishti-10 UAV is based on Israeli Elbit Systems' Hermes-900 platform
Crash occurred near Porbandar, Gujarat during a training sortie
No loss of life; Court of Inquiry ordered by Indian Navy
Second mishap involving this platform; used for maritime surveillance

title: US-Iran Conflict Escalates: Iran Fires 10 Ballistic Missiles at Jordan's Azraq Base; US Ceasefire Ends
summary: Iran fired ten ballistic missiles at the Azraq military base in Jordan, which hosts a US military command centre, marking one of the most intense strikes since the ceasefire between the US and Iran. The US declared the ceasefire was over, and fighter jets escorted Ayatollah Khamenei's coffin for burial in Mashhad, indicating regime leadership change dynamics. President Trump stated Iran had placed him at the top of a 'kill list'. Russia simultaneously banned diesel exports following Ukrainian drone strikes on its refineries, further straining global energy markets.
exam_angle: The US-Iran conflict and its impact on global oil prices, India's energy security, and the Middle East geopolitical order are critical for GS Paper 2 (IR) and GS Paper 3 (Economy/Energy Security).
key_facts: Iran fired 10 ballistic missiles at Azraq military base, Jordan (US command centre)
US declared end of ceasefire with Iran
Ayatollah Khamenei killed; burial at Mashhad's Imam Reza shrine
Russia banned diesel exports following Ukrainian drone strikes on refineries

title: IMF and ADB Trim India's Growth Forecast Citing High Crude Oil Prices
summary: Both the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the Asian Development Bank (ADB) have revised downward their growth forecasts for India, citing elevated global crude oil prices as a key risk. High crude prices raise India's import bill, widen the current account deficit, and stoke inflation, thereby dampening growth. This comes amid ongoing US-Iran tensions that have kept global oil markets volatile.
exam_angle: India's macroeconomic vulnerability to crude oil price shocks is a standard GS Paper 3 (Economy) topic. IMF and ADB forecasts, current account deficit, and inflation linkage are important concepts.
key_facts: Both IMF and ADB revised India's GDP growth forecast downward
Reason cited: high global crude oil prices
High crude raises import bill, widens current account deficit, fuels inflation
US-Iran tensions a major driver of crude price volatility

title: India Removes Import Duty on Select Smartphone and Electronics Components
summary: The Indian government has removed import duty on select smartphone and electronics parts, a move aimed at boosting domestic electronics manufacturing competitiveness and supporting the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for mobile phones. The duty reduction is expected to lower input costs for manufacturers and make India more attractive as a global electronics hub. This is consistent with India's broader strategy to become a leading electronics exporter.
exam_angle: Customs duty rationalisation, PLI scheme for electronics, and India's strategy to become a global electronics manufacturing hub are key GS Paper 3 (Economy/Industry) topics.
key_facts: Import duty removed on select smartphone and electronics parts
Supports PLI scheme for mobile phone manufacturing
Aims to lower input costs and boost electronics exports
Part of India's 'Make in India' electronics manufacturing push

title: India's E20 Ethanol-Blended Fuel Programme: Controversy and Gadkari's Defence
summary: India's programme to blend 20% ethanol in petrol (E20) has sparked public controversy, with vehicle owners and protesters alleging damage to engines, especially older two-wheelers, and claiming that oil companies are making 'illegitimate profits'. Union Minister Nitin Gadkari defended the E20 rollout, calling it essential for energy security and reducing fossil fuel imports. Protesters challenged Gadkari to present evidence of a single vehicle damaged by ethanol, while he invited them to present evidence of damage.
exam_angle: India's ethanol blending programme (National Biofuel Policy 2018, E20 target by 2025-26) is a critical GS Paper 3 (Environment/Economy) topic linking energy security, agriculture, and biofuels.
key_facts: E20 = 20% ethanol blended with 80% petrol; India's target under National Biofuel Policy
Nitin Gadkari (Union Minister for Road Transport) is the key proponent
Controversy: older vehicle owners allege engine damage from high ethanol content
E20 aims to reduce fossil fuel import dependence and cut carbon emissions

title: Supreme Court to Examine if Arrest Memo Typographical Error Can Justify Bail — Meghalaya Honeymoon Murder Case
summary: The Supreme Court is examining a significant legal question: whether a typographical error in an arrest memo can serve as grounds for granting bail to an accused person. The case relates to the Meghalaya honeymoon murder case involving Sonam Raghuvanshi. The Court is considering referring the matter to a larger constitutional bench, indicating the issue has wider legal implications for procedural rights of accused persons under the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) / Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).
exam_angle: Rights of the accused, procedural safeguards under CrPC/BNSS (arrest memo requirements), and Supreme Court's power to refer matters to larger benches are important for GS Paper 2 (Polity/Governance) and GS Paper 4 (Ethics/Rule of Law).
key_facts: SC examining if arrest memo typo justifies bail — Sonam Raghuvanshi (Meghalaya honeymoon murder case)
SC considering reference to a larger constitutional bench
Arrest memo is a procedural requirement under CrPC/BNSS at the time of arrest
Raises questions about procedural rights vs. substantive justice

title: FBI Unravels Lawrence Bishnoi Gang Network; 'Operation Hardball' Targets Bishnoi-Brar Network
summary: The US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) used undercover agents and informants to dismantle Lawrence Bishnoi gang's operations in North America, as revealed by the US Department of Justice (DoJ). The chargesheet also revealed that slain Khalistani militant Hardeep Singh Nijjar had persuaded gangster Arsh Dalla to flee to Canada. A separate 'Operation Hardball' by Indian agencies is targeting the Bishnoi-Brar network. The US DoJ noted Bishnoi ran a decentralised syndicate and sought to instil fear through targeted killings.
exam_angle: The nexus between Khalistani terrorism, organised crime networks (Bishnoi, Brar, Dalla), and their cross-border operations is important for GS Paper 3 (Internal Security) and GS Paper 2 (IR — Canada-India relations).
key_facts: FBI used undercover agents and informants to dismantle Lawrence Bishnoi's North America network
US DoJ: Bishnoi ran a decentralised syndicate targeting Indian nationals abroad
Hardeep Singh Nijjar persuaded gangster Arsh Dalla to flee to Canada (NDTV chargesheet)
'Operation Hardball' — Indian agency operation targeting Bishnoi-Brar network

title: Wayanad Landslide Toll Rises to Six; Concerns Renewed Over Landslide Risk in India
summary: The death toll in a fresh landslide in Kalladi village, Wayanad district, Kerala rose to six as three more bodies were recovered. The incident has renewed concerns over landslide risks in India, particularly in the Western Ghats region which is ecologically sensitive. Wayanad witnessed a catastrophic landslide in July 2024 that killed over 400 people. Experts link recurring landslides to deforestation, encroachment in ecologically sensitive zones, and extreme rainfall events intensified by climate change.
exam_angle: Landslide vulnerability in India (especially Western Ghats), the Geological Survey of India's Landslide Atlas, and the link between climate change, deforestation, and disaster frequency are important for GS Paper 1 (Geography) and GS Paper 3 (Disaster Management/Environment).
key_facts: Landslide location: Kalladi, Wayanad, Kerala
Toll rose to 6 deaths; rescue mission in final phase
Western Ghats is an Ecologically Sensitive Area (ESA) — Gadgil and Kasturirangan reports relevant
Wayanad had India's deadliest landslide in July 2024 (400+ deaths)

title: Gujarat Launches First Data Centre Policy; Targets ₹6 Lakh Crore Investment and 7.5 GW Capacity
summary: Gujarat has launched its first-ever Data Centre Policy, setting ambitious targets of attracting ₹6 lakh crore in investments and developing 7.5 GW of data centre capacity. The policy aims to make Gujarat a leading destination for data centre infrastructure in India, in line with the national push for digital infrastructure. The move follows India's rapid data consumption growth and the increasing need for cloud and AI computing infrastructure.
exam_angle: Data centre policy, digital infrastructure development, state-level investment policies, and India's data governance framework are relevant for GS Paper 3 (Economy/Sci-Tech) and GS Paper 2 (Governance).
key_facts: Gujarat launched its first Data Centre Policy (2026)
Investment target: ₹6 lakh crore
Capacity target: 7.5 GW of data centre infrastructure
Aimed at making Gujarat India's leading data centre hub

title: India Gets World's First Once-a-Week Insulin 'Awiqli' by Novo Nordisk
summary: India has received approval for and access to 'Awiqli', the world's first once-a-week insulin developed by Danish pharmaceutical company Novo Nordisk. Awiqli (insulin icodec) is a basal insulin analogue that replaces the need for daily insulin injections in Type 2 diabetes patients, offering a major improvement in patient adherence and quality of life. India has among the world's largest populations of diabetes patients, making this a significant public health development.
exam_angle: Drug approvals, pharmaceutical innovation, and India's diabetes burden (second-largest globally) are important for GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech/Health). The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) approval process is also relevant.
key_facts: Drug name: Awiqli (insulin icodec) — world's first once-a-week basal insulin
Developed by: Novo Nordisk (Denmark)
Indicated for: Type 2 diabetes patients requiring basal insulin therapy
India has ~100 million diabetic patients — world's second-largest diabetes population

title: Digital India BHASHINI Division and NFSU Sign MoU to Advance Multilingual AI and Language Technologies
summary: The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD) under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU) to collaborate on multilingual AI and language technologies. BHASHINI is India's national language translation mission that aims to make digital services accessible in all Indian languages. The MoU will focus on applying AI-driven language tools to forensic sciences and law enforcement.
exam_angle: BHASHINI mission (language AI for Indian languages), MeitY's digital India initiatives, and AI governance/applications are important for GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech) and GS Paper 2 (Governance/Digital India).
key_facts: MoU signed between Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD) and National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU)
BHASHINI: India's national AI-based language translation mission under MeitY
Focus: Multilingual AI tools for forensic sciences and law enforcement
NFSU is India's first university dedicated to forensic sciences, headquartered in Gandhinagar, Gujarat

title: BSE Turns 151: Asia's Oldest Stock Exchange Milestones
summary: The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) completed 151 years of operations, marking a significant milestone for Asia's oldest stock exchange. Established in 1875 as the Native Share and Stock Brokers' Association, BSE was the first stock exchange in Asia and has evolved into one of the world's largest exchanges by number of listed companies. It operates the SENSEX index (30 blue-chip companies) and is regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).
exam_angle: BSE's history, SEBI's regulatory role, and Indian capital markets are standard GS Paper 3 (Economy) topics. The founding year and Asia-first status are frequently asked facts.
key_facts: BSE (Bombay Stock Exchange) established in 1875 — Asia's oldest stock exchange
Originally called: Native Share and Stock Brokers' Association
BSE celebrates 151st anniversary in 2026
Regulator: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI); benchmark index: SENSEX

title: India's TCS Q1 FY27 Revenue Beats Estimates Aided by Weak Rupee and Banking Sector Boost
summary: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), India's largest IT company, reported Q1 FY2026-27 revenues that exceeded market estimates, driven by a weak Indian rupee (which boosts rupee-denominated revenues from dollar-earning exports) and strong demand from the banking, financial services, and insurance (BFSI) sector. This comes amid broader concerns about AI-driven 'silent layoffs' in India's IT sector, with approximately 35,000 tech jobs potentially eliminated in 2026 due to automation and AI deployment.
exam_angle: India's IT sector performance, impact of rupee depreciation on IT exports, and AI-driven employment disruption are important for GS Paper 3 (Economy/Technology). TCS as a bellwether for the sector is significant.
key_facts: TCS Q1 FY27 revenue beat estimates; aided by weak rupee and BFSI sector demand
India's IT sector faces ~35,000 job eliminations in 2026 due to AI automation ('silent layoffs')
TCS is India's largest IT company by revenue and market capitalisation
Weak rupee benefits IT exporters by increasing rupee value of dollar revenues

title: Destination Tripura Business Conclave 2026: Union Minister Scindia Invites Investment in Tripura
summary: Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia invited investors to explore Tripura's growth potential at the 'Destination Tripura Business Conclave 2026', signalling the government's focus on developing the northeastern states through investment promotion. The conclave is part of the broader 'Act East Policy' and the PM's vision of developing the Northeast as India's growth engine. Tripura shares borders with Bangladesh and has strategic connectivity advantages via Agartala-Akhaura rail link.
exam_angle: Investment conclaves for Northeast India, Act East Policy, and PM-DevINE scheme for northeastern development are relevant for GS Paper 2 (Governance/IR) and GS Paper 3 (Economy).
key_facts: Event: Destination Tripura Business Conclave 2026
Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia (Ministry of Communications) invited investors
Tripura borders Bangladesh; connected via Agartala-Akhaura rail link
Aligns with Act East Policy and PM-DevINE scheme for Northeast

title: India Gets 98th Chess Grandmaster — Aswath S
summary: Aswath S has become India's 98th Chess Grandmaster (GM), adding to India's growing dominance in international chess. Both of Aswath's parents are chess coaches, and his journey to the GM title overcame challenges including a forced break during his Class 10 board examinations. India has been a chess powerhouse in recent years, with D. Gukesh becoming the youngest-ever World Chess Champion in 2024 and the country hosting the 2024 Chess Olympiad in Chennai.
exam_angle: India's chess achievements and persons in news related to sports and awards are standard GS Paper topics. The number of Indian GMs is frequently updated and asked in exams.
key_facts: Aswath S becomes India's 98th Chess Grandmaster
India is the country with the most chess Grandmasters globally
D. Gukesh (India) became youngest-ever World Chess Champion in December 2024
India hosted Chess Olympiad 2024 in Chennai

title: India Sets July 15 Deadline for LA 2028 Olympics Athlete Selection Criteria
summary: India has set a deadline of July 15, 2026 for finalising athlete selection criteria for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games. This move by the relevant sports federations and the Sports Authority of India (SAI) / Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports aims to provide clarity and transparency in the athlete qualification process well in advance. The 2028 Olympics are scheduled in Los Angeles, USA.
exam_angle: Olympics athlete selection policy, role of SAI and national sports federations, and governance of sports in India are relevant for GS Paper 2 (Governance) and general awareness.
key_facts: Deadline set: July 15, 2026 for LA 2028 Olympic athlete selection criteria
LA 2028 Olympics: Los Angeles, USA (July–August 2028)
Nodal ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports; implementing body: SAI
Aimed at transparency and early planning for Olympic qualification
